values.note: $20 a single site, $40 a double site. recreation.gov charges the same in its first-come seasons (May 1-21 and Sep 7-27, 2026). The Forest Service page also lists an 'Additional Vehicle Fee: $7 per vehicle' beside its '$10 fee for extra 2nd vehicle'; recreation.gov says $10 a night, collected at the campground.

fees.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r04/bridger-teton/recreation/atherton-creek-campground ('Single Site: $20 per night | Double Site: $40 per night', '$10 fee for extra 2nd vehicle, no more than 2 vehicles/ site') + https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/10351635/rates (Peak Season 2026-05-22 to 2026-09-06: PeakStandard 20, two double types 40; 2027 identical) + rec.gov notice ('Extra vehicle will be charged a $10 per night fee and collected at the campground'), read 2026-11-20

values.note: 21 sites, 16 of them reservable. The reservable catalog types 14 sites for RV/trailer (back-in driveways 30-90 ft, most 55-65 ft) and two (A24, A26, 25 and 40 ft) for tents, pickup campers and camper vans only. recreation.gov calls the sites 'suitable for tents and smaller trailers'; no length limit is posted.

sites.source: https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/10351635 ('Atherton Campground has 21 standard sites (16 are available for reservation), suitable for tents and smaller trailers') + recreation.gov campsite search for 10351635 (per-site permitted equipment and Driveway Length), read 2026-11-20

values.note: Closes September 22 each year: water off, toilets locked, no trash. The gate stays open and the campground may be used free once every amenity is off (half price if only water is on). recreation.gov's first-come rate season starts May 1.

season.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r04/bridger-teton/recreation/atherton-creek-campground (Operational Hours: 'Campground closes on the 22nd of September, annually', 'the gate will not be closed, and campground can still be used for no fee when all amenities are turned off') + rec.gov rates (First-come, First-served Season 2026-05-01 to 2026-05-21), read 2026-11-20

values.note: 16 of 21 sites reservable in the peak season (May 22 - Sep 6, 2026); the rest first-come, and the whole campground is first-come May 1-21 and Sep 7-27.

booking.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r04/bridger-teton/recreation/atherton-creek-campground ('Campsites are a mix of reservable and first come, first served') + rec.gov description and rate seasons, read 2026-11-20

note: Bridger-Teton NF campground on Lower Slide Lake in the Gros Ventre near Kelly, paved access. The loops sit on a grassy bench above the lake behind a band of shoreline trees and shrubs; the campground has no public lake access. One site (A21) has electric. --Claude
summary: FS page + rec.gov 10351635: confirmed $20/$40 (single/double), 16 of 21 reservable (fcfs some_sites), vault toilets, electric only at A21 (30/50); count 18->21 (FS says 20, rec.gov 21), cleared unsourced 30-ft max (driveways 30-90 ft), added season close Sep 22 and $10 extra vehicle. lakeview confirmed on imagery (nearest RV sites ~20-40 m from the beach line through a continuous tree/shrub band). Pin ~45 m from the site centroid, fine.
flags: Missing phone: empty -> 307-739-5400 (Jackson Ranger District office, on the FS page and rec.gov; the FS page's 'Contact Phone' line gives 307-739-5500, the Supervisor's Office).

Potable water conflict: the FS page's amenity block says 'Potable water is not available at this site' while its Operational Hours line says 'Campground will have water turned off ... If only water is on, fees are 1/2 price' and rec.gov lists a 'Water Spigot'. potable_water left unset.

RIG-LENGTH wording: rec.gov describes the sites as 'suitable for tents and smaller trailers'. No length is posted; the catalog permits RV and Trailer on 14 reservable sites with back-in driveways 30-90 ft (A01 80, A10 90, A07/A09/A11 60), and imagery shows several full-size motorhomes and fifth-wheels on the loop. Read as no bar to a 23-ft rig; no review checked.

Waterfront lakeview confirmed: nearest sites (A15 at 43.63712,-110.52488, and an unnumbered first-come site just west of it) sit ~20-40 m from the beach line but behind a continuous band of trees and shrubs; the upper meadow loop (A07-A12, A18-A19) looks across open grass over the trees to the lake ~80-150 m away. rec.gov: 'No public lake access through the campground.' No on-water upgrade.
Electric: the derived 50 rests on one reservable site, A21 (30/50); rec.gov's description and the FS page mention no hookups. The site is publicly bookable, so kept.
rec.gov facility record carries a wrong point (43.3815, 110.3123, sign dropped and ~28 km off); the FS page gives 43.638548,-110.522141, beside the loop.
